name: Prize crossword No 23,717
preamble: Solve the clues and fit solutions into the diagram wherever they will go, jigsaw-wise.

clue.text: Elevator with excursionist concealing male criminal

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a jack is a device that lifts a car
a tripper is someone on a day excursion
the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A lift attendant and a day-tripper are harbouring a male crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevator' looks like a lift, but here it is the car jack. The tripper wraps around the male pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian Whitechapel murderer is the most notorious unidentified killer in British history.

clue.text: Hermit finds security and with it ecstasy

blocks.note: an anchor is a source of security or stability
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A recluse discovers safety and, with it, rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy here is the drug, abbreviated to its street name E.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious recluse who withdraws from society, a synonym for a solitary devotee.

clue.text: "Up," observed monarch, "up with the dance"

definitions.note: the answer is the word that, put with 'up', names the dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending letters up makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: observed means seen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king gives orders to rise and join the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is a lively British party with dancing, so the answer plus 'up' makes the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Knees-up is colloquial British for a boisterous celebration with dancing, so this word completes that compound.

clue.text: Higher chopper, say, for beast of the rocks

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak the phrase and hear what it sounds like

blocks.note: a chopper is an axe, and a higher one is a 'higher axe'

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a raised axe for some mountain animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The rock hyrax is the common species, which makes 'beast of the rocks' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyrax is a small furry African mammal that lives among boulders and rocky outcrops.

clue.text: Borrow book by red man without a lot of point

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the Gaelic name Rory means red king
many means a lot of
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A borrowed book is by a red-skinned man, missing much of the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' is not a verb but George Borrow, the Victorian writer; 'red man' is the name Rory, Gaelic for red king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romany Rye is George Borrow's 1857 novel, a sequel to Lavengro, about Gypsy life.

clue.text: Resonance of scheme by General Grant

blocks.note: a scheme is a plan
GEN is the abbreviation for general
Cy Grant was a Guyanese-born singer and actor well known on British television

explanation.surface: The echo of a strategy devised by the American Civil War general Ulysses Grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General Grant' reads as the American commander, but it splits into the rank and the first name of Cy Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangency is a loud, deep, ringing quality of sound, close in sense to resonance.

clue.text: Not the all-American girl

indicators.note: not the whole of a word means only a part of it is wanted

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: This girl is not the typical all-American sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-American' sounds like a compliment, but 'Not the all' asks for only part of 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a female given name, so it fits a general reference to a girl.

clue.text: Vitality after questions by good girl with monocle

indicators.note: coming after means placed behind, so the order is set by this word

blocks.note: to quiz is to question
zing is energy or vitality
G is the abbreviation for good
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A well-behaved girl wearing an eyeglass answers questions with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue starts with the second piece; 'after' puts it behind the questions.
explanation.definitionFit: A quizzing-glass was an eighteenth-century single eyeglass, essentially a monocle on a handle or ribbon.

clue.text: Log recreating wind, terror etc

indicators.note: to recreate something is to make it afresh, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's log recounts gales, fear and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a ship's log of storms, but it is all letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A log is a formal written account of events kept in order, as aboard a ship.

clue.text: Relative to a relative's initially obscure

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something about one family member's connection to another is hazy at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' appears twice: first it is a family member, then only its first letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure is hard to make out or understand, which is exactly what this word describes.

clue.text: Comparatively substantial body, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a meteor is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A rumour that a fairly large corpse has turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body' suggests a corpse or physique, but here it is a heavenly body, a meteor.
explanation.definitionFit: Meatier is the comparative of meaty, meaning having more substance or solid content.

clue.text: Gad! It's grand among lots of animals

definitions.note: the answer is the oath that completes Gadzooks, and is itself an oath

indicators.note: to be among things is to sit in their midst, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: zoos are collections of animals
a grand is a thousand, abbreviated K

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a fine sight in a menagerie.
explanation.walkthrough: Gad and zooks are both old mild oaths, and together they make Gadzooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Zooks is an archaic exclamation of surprise, a shortened form of the oath Gadzooks.

clue.text: Apple inserted into orange, possibly, within 10 feet

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters
within means inside, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
taken as written
FT is the abbreviation for feet

explanation.surface: A gardener grafts an apple onto an orange tree.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is the Roman numeral. The definition reuses 'orange' from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A xenograft is tissue transplanted between different species, like grafting one fruit tree onto another kind.

clue.text: Return of some news-papers provides epic

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters run backwards
only some of the word is wanted, so part of it is dropped

blocks.note: dailies are newspapers; the last two letters of that word go

explanation.surface: Bringing back a few newspapers yields a heroic tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'news-papers' is a red herring; the word wanted is dailies, trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad is Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War, the classic example of the genre.

clue.text: Old coin for little boy, pickpocket and deserter

blocks.note: Dan is a short form of Daniel, a boy's name
dip is slang for a pickpocket
a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: An antique coin is handed over for a child, a thief and a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: Dandiprat also means a small boy, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandiprat was a small silver coin of sixteenth-century England, worth three halfpence.

clue.text: Dance in Provence (a long way off) and in Spain (Bravo!)

blocks.note: far means a long way off
taken as written
olé is the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: A dance performed in southern France, far away, and cheered in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed asides look like travel notes, but each gives a piece in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The farandole is a traditional Provençal chain dance in which dancers hold hands and wind through streets.

clue.text: What's said about V in 4 is on V

definitions.note: V stands for the Victoria Cross, and the definition is the inscription on it

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another
in means inside, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: the number written as a word
oral means spoken
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a letter V placed in a number.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference but is simply the word four. V stands for the Victoria Cross, which bears the motto.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word motto engraved on the Victoria Cross, Britain's highest military award for gallantry.

clue.text: Muslins when the music stops

blocks.note: first meaning: fine sheer cotton fabrics
second meaning, read as two words: the keyboard instrument falls silent

explanation.surface: Fabrics for a party dress when the dancing ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer reads 'organ dies', which is when the music stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiffened, translucent cotton, a type of muslin used for dresses.

clue.text: Leafy growth provides room in theatre for actor

indicators.note: providing one thing for another means swapping it in as a replacement

blocks.note: the green room is where performers wait offstage; its 'room' is the part replaced
Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.surface: Plant life gives an actor space in a playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap 'room' in green room for the actor Tree. Beerbohm Tree founded RADA and built Her Majesty's Theatre in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree in leaf is green, so a green tree is literally a growth covered in leaves.

clue.text: Huntsman could be a grey

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests one possible version of the letters, not their given order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunt rider might be on a grey horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A grey is a horse, which suits the hunting picture, but the words are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yager, from German Jäger, means a hunter, and was used for riflemen recruited from huntsmen.

clue.text: Oil from crab until cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Fat rendered from a crab while it is being cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' and 'crab' make a kitchen picture, but the oil is for machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is the commonest substance applied to reduce friction between moving parts.

clue.text: First whaling captain elevated by religion

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters makes them read from the bottom up

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so first
Captain Ahab hunts the whale in Moby-Dick

explanation.surface: The first whaling skipper was uplifted by faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like it describes the captain, but it is the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bahá'í Faith is a monotheistic religion founded in nineteenth-century Persia by Bahá'u'lláh.

clue.text: Friendly place to dress around pole

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a toga is a Roman garment
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A welcoming spot to get dressed around a maypole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' has a capital meaning hidden by its position: Captain Cook named Tonga the Friendly Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook, so it is literally a Friendly place.

clue.text: Section would be funny with change of heart

indicators.note: changing the heart means swapping the central letter for another

blocks.note: comic means funny; its middle letter is replaced

explanation.surface: A part of something would be amusing if it changed its mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle M becomes N. A conic is a conic section, the curve made by slicing a cone.
explanation.definitionFit: Conic is short for conic section, a curve such as an ellipse formed where a plane cuts a cone.

clue.text: Provide for queens

definitions.note: read as cat-er: one who is all for queens, that is female cats

blocks.note: first meaning: supply food or what is needed
second meaning, whimsically: a cat-lover, since a queen is a female cat

explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat, so one who is all for queens is a cat-er, read as cat plus -er.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply provisions or services, a direct synonym for providing.

clue.text: Singer in South Australia backs lively movement

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other pieces
to go backwards is to run the letters the other way

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
Cher is the American pop singer
Oz is the nickname for Australia

explanation.surface: A vocalist down under supports a spirited new trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Australia' reads as the state, but it splits into S and Oz, and only Oz turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a quick, playful section of a symphony or sonata, so a brisk musical movement.

clue.text: Comparatively dapper painter

blocks.note: first meaning: smarter in dress
second meaning: an eighteenth-century French portraitist at the court of Louis XV

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of an artist's clothes, but they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and neat, so the comparative form fits; Nattier also painted the French court.

clue.text: Hero's "we are not amused"?

definitions.note: possessive: what a hero has, the decoration

blocks.note: first meaning: the highest British award for gallantry, which a hero wears
second meaning: the line attributed to the old Queen, said when she was annoyed

explanation.walkthrough: "We are not amused" is the line attributed to Queen Victoria, so she was cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military gallantry award, and a cross Victoria is an annoyed queen.
